page: Amazon Web Services r6gd.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton2 processor using Neoverse-N1 cores. The configuration provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz, eliminating hyper-threading contention through a 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation. System memory is sized at 256.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio with 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is directly attached via 1900 GB of NVMe SSD instance storage, supplemented by a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps without dedicated graphics accelerators.

Benchmark data displays solid multi-threaded performance alongside lower single-threaded metrics. The instance achieved 11391.0 in Geekbench multi-core testing and 48584.58 in stress-ng multi-core, reflecting balanced parallel processing across all 32 dedicated cores. Conversely, single-threaded execution is a relative bottleneck, registering a Geekbench single-core score of 933.0 and reduced throughput on single-threaded compression algorithms such as bzip3 (6.62 GB/sec). Memory throughput remains steady, delivering 150.22 GB/sec in large-block uncached reads and sustaining 38.98 million Redis SET operations per second.

The integration of 1900 GB high-speed NVMe local storage paired with an ARM architecture provides significant resource density and cost efficiency for large-footprint applications. Operating cost efficiency is prioritized by utilizing custom ARM silicon that delivers lower power consumption per core than equivalent x86 instances, though workloads requiring specialized vector instruction sets such as AVX-512 are not supported. The instance is suited for in-memory databases, Redis caches, high-throughput key-value stores, distributed data processing, and transient ETL pipelines requiring high IOPS local scratch space.
description: Amazon Web Services r6gd.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance driven by a 32-core AWS Graviton2 ARM Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro System, it allocates 32 dedicated physical cores with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio and 256.0 GB of RAM, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes 1900 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 12 Gbps, without an integrated GPU. Benchmark evaluations reveal consistent multi-core performance, achieving 48584.58 in multi-threaded stress-ng and 38.98 million Redis SET operations per second, offset by modest single-threaded throughput. Due to its combination of high-density memory, local NVMe scratch storage, and energy-efficient ARM compute, the r6gd.8xlarge is suited for in-memory caching, distributed database workloads, and data-intensive ETL jobs.
